official_measurement_examples.name: England coverage
official_measurement_examples.fact: Defra states 48 LNRS areas cover all of England with no gaps or overlaps.

official_measurement_examples.name: 26 June 2026 status update
official_measurement_examples.fact: Defra updated the national status list on 26 June 2026 and recorded Warwickshire, West Sussex and East Sussex and Brighton & Hove as published.

official_measurement_examples.name: Strategy role
official_measurement_examples.fact: LNRS maps priorities and opportunities for nature recovery; it does not itself grant planning permission or establish development capacity.

official_measurement_examples.name: Biodiversity duty
official_measurement_examples.fact: Public authorities in England must have regard to relevant LNRS when complying with the strengthened biodiversity duty.

official_measurement_examples.name: Local tailoring
official_measurement_examples.fact: Each LNRS is locally led and specific to its strategy area, so one strategy must not be applied outside its geographic scope.

official_measurement_examples.name: Map proposals
official_measurement_examples.fact: Mapped recovery opportunities identify where action may be especially useful but are not compulsory land-use designations by themselves.

official_measurement_examples.name: BNG distinction
official_measurement_examples.fact: LNRS information can interact with biodiversity planning but does not replace statutory BNG calculations or other protected-site controls.

official_measurement_examples.name: Temporal status
official_measurement_examples.fact: Draft, consultation and published strategy states must be retained separately and not silently merged.

core_rules: LNRS opportunity mapping is not planning permission
LNRS opportunity mapping is not a statutory ownership boundary
draft LNRS content must not be treated as adopted strategy
published status must retain update date
one LNRS must not be applied outside its strategy area
LNRS opportunity is not proof habitat creation is feasible on a parcel
LNRS does not replace protected-site assessment
LNRS does not replace statutory BNG calculations
biodiversity duty does not create private access rights
mapped nature opportunity does not determine land ownership
local strategy evidence must retain local authority provenance
absence of a mapped opportunity is not proof no biodiversity constraint exists
historic strategy versions must not silently override newer publication status
LNRS evidence does not reserve development capacity
no parcel LNRS clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
